# GitHub Copilot Instructions

## Documentation Structure

This file provides GitHub Copilot-specific coding instructions. For comprehensive project documentation:

- **AGENTS.md**: Master documentation for all AI coding services (architecture, workflows, build pipelines, etc.)
- **algorithm.md**: Technical algorithm documentation (zh-Hant-TW)

**Note:** GitHub Copilot does not automatically read AGENTS.md files. Essential guidelines are included below.

---

## General Guidelines

- **Language restriction:** Use only English or zh-Hant-TW in all documentation, comments, and reviews. An exception is that `zh-Hans` is allowed in any file name stem ended with `-CHS`, where the required style is **zh-Hans-TW**: simplify the characters only and keep Taiwan vocabulary (e.g. `支援` stays `支援`, never `支持`). Other exceptions may be given by the developer.

## Project Context
- Input method for macOS built with AppKit/IMKit in Swift, backed by statistic-based language models loaded into `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/Sources/LexiconAssembly` module.
- The current mainline sentence assembler is `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/Sources/Homa`, which replaced the old Megrez runtime path during a big surgery in late April 2026 while keeping the same DAG-DP design direction.
- If you are on Linux or Windows NT, your only workspace is `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard` and its dependencies situated in `./Packages`. If you are on Windows, you can also work with `./Packages/vChewing_MainAssembly4Darwin` and its dependencies situated in `./Packages` folder. Note that the session system (`InputSession`, `SessionProtocol`, `SessionHost`, etc.) now lives in `vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard` — session-involving development is possible on Linux/Windows, with all OS-dependent actions injected via `SessionHost` closures.
- Lexicon assets are provided by remote Swift Package plugin `VanguardTextMapPlugin` (from `vChewing-VanguardLexicon` repository) and compiled at build-time as `.txtMap` / `.revlookup` pairs, then injected into `vChewing_MainAssembly4Darwin`.
- Tests are written among local Swift Packages situated in `./Packages/` folder. Tests are usually implemented on a case-by-case basis when an issue case comes out: Write a new test case to confirm the bug exists. 
- Preserve the existing MulanPSL-2.0 license banner on any new Swift source file (build-side files such as `Package*.swift` manifests and `makefile`s are not Swift sources and take no banner), except certain local Swift Packages licensed with things other than MulanPSL-2.0.

## OS Framework Guidelines
- All AppKit windows are supposed to be constructed using AppKit Result Builder DSL. You can find its definitions in `./Packages/vChewing_OSFrameworkImpl/`.
- Study the `UserDef` enum which manages raw UserDefaults keys with their data types and localization keys (used in the SettingsUI and SettingsCocoa window). If you extended `UserDef`, please also extend `PrefMgrProtocol` and `PrefMgr`. Direct access to UserDefaults are discouraged in most times unless really necessary.
- Localize UI strings with `NSLocalizedString("…", comment: "")` and update the localization assets (`.strings`) files. Note that `xcstring` assets can also be considered in the future if it is compatible with targets compiled for macOS 12.
- Follow the established flow: the portable `InputSession` (in `vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard`) is bound by `SessionControllerSputnik.swift` to IMK's `IMKInputSessionController` from `vChewing_IMKUtils`; `InputSession_DarwinSurface.swift` converts NSEvents to KBEvents and forwards them to the session core; the session handles KeyUp events and lets `InputHandler` triage KeyDown events (as KBEvent); `IMEState` models state transitions.
- Do not dispatch the UI-related things to an async thread unless it is on the main actor.

## FSM Design
- Convert incoming NSEvents to KBEvents and let them triaged by `InputHandler`. This allows state transitions happen pass places and UI response flow with state changes.
- In most cases you don't need to extend the state machine. If you really have to, you can extend the state machine by adding new `IMEState` type enum cases plus explicit state transition APIs; bypass the existing states using booleans is discouraged, and you only use it whenever really necessary.

## Objective-C(++) & C(++) Guidelines
- There are no bridging headers for Xcode. However, some Objective-C(++) & C(++) contents are used in some Swift Package dependency targets for purposes not-directly-achievable in Swift.
- Always use Google Format of Style for Objective-C(++) & C(++).

## Tests and Tooling
- GitHub Coding Agent can only access Linux devenv in most times. `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/` is the Linux-compilable target that the developer usually ask GitHub Coding Agent to work on. This package and `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/Sources/Homa/` are the primary places to add migration-related tests.
- Factory lexicons come from the separate `vChewing-VanguardLexicon` repository in Vanguard TextMap format (`.txtMap` + `.revlookup`), injected into `vChewing_MainAssembly4Darwin` at build time by the remote `VanguardTextMapPlugin` Swift Package plugin (no git submodule). The legacy `CSQLite3` dependency has been fully removed from this repository; Yahoo KeyKey data import in `vChewing_OtherIMEDataReader` now uses the system libsqlite3. Regenerate lexicon assets via `make update` when explicitly instructed.

## Git Commit Convention

- Use Conventional Commits format for all commits and pull requests.
- Format: `ModuleName // SubModuleName: Changes-described.`
- Example: `LibVanguard // Patch the codepoint converter for Linux.`
- Keep descriptions concise.
- Reference: https://www.conventionalcommits.org/

## Build System & CLI

- **Primary**: `make release` (universal arm64 + x86_64 with App Sandbox entitlements, hardened runtime, codesigned).
- **Alternative**: `make archive` (same but also creates `.xcarchive` with dSYMs for distribution).
- **Debug**: `make debug` (single native architecture, faster iteration).
- **Internals**: Makefile orchestrates per-arch Swift builds, lipo merge, lexicon assembly, and invokes `BundleApps` CommandPlugin for app bundle creation and signing. The Swift 5.10 legacy path adds `debugLegacy` (one x86_64 slice at macOS 10.9) / `releaseLegacy` (the same slice plus an `arm64-apple-macosx11.0` one, `lipo`ed into universal executables) and `cleanLegacy`; both build targets finish by assembling their own bundles (`$(MAKE) bundleLegacy LEGACY_CONFIG=<cfg>`), since the two configurations share one `Build/Products/Legacy/` and a hand-run `make bundleLegacy` defaults to `debug`. Both also pass `-Xlinker -platform_version -Xlinker macos -Xlinker <min> -Xlinker <sdkVersion>` (version read from `$(LEGACY_SDK)/SDKSettings.plist`) because SwiftPM 5.10 otherwise fills that slot from the triple, leaving the executables claiming `sdk 10.9` while linked against 13.3 — AppKit reads that field to decide whether an app is old enough to be locked into Aqua, which is why `vChewingInstallerLegacy` had no dark mode (the IME was saved by its `NSRequiresAquaSystemAppearance` key), plus the `BundleAppsLegacy` plugin, which embeds the back-deployment Swift runtime collected from the installed Xcodes and adds a fallback rpath (`@loader_path/Frameworks`) so that old systems use those copies while the current one keeps using the system runtime; `make bundleLegacy` additionally assembles `Build/Products/Legacy/vChewing.app` and `vChewingInstallerLegacy.app`, each carrying that runtime in `Contents/Frameworks/` behind `@executable_path/../Frameworks`, and stamps both Info.plists with the `DT*` build-environment keys Xcode normally writes (`DTXcode`, `DTSDKBuild`, `DTSDKName`, `DTPlatformVersion`, `BuildMachineOSBuild`, …) by reading the platform's own template at `<sdk>/../../Info.plist` → `AdditionalInfo` (a Command Line Tools SDK has no platform around it, so there the plugin falls back to the *active* developer directory's platform via `xcode-select -p`, which honours `DEVELOPER_DIR`) and resolving its `$(…)` variables from the SDK passed as `--sdk` (`make bundleLegacy` passes `LEGACY_SDK`; without it the bundles carry no such record), while `LSMinimumSystemVersion` stays pinned to `legacyDeploymentTarget` rather than being copied from that template. Its assembly also drops the absolute `LC_RPATH` entries naming the build machine's toolchain. Note that the 5.10 closure has held zero concurrency references since 2026-09-16 (0 of 20 archives per slice), so `libswift_Concurrency` appears in no load command — the collected copy is now unused headroom, deliberately left in place per the owner's call (2026-09-16). `CGRect.seniorTheBeast` is likewise a file-private constant at the bottom of each consuming file — never a shared `SwiftExtension` one — and the legacy repo mirrors that arrangement file-for-file. The plugin also merges `LegacyZone/InstallerLocalizations/<lproj>/InfoPlist.strings` over the localization directories it copies, so the legacy installer shows a different localized name in Finder than the modern one even though both draw on a single source `<lproj>` set (the IME's mirror-image override sits in `LegacyZone/IMELocalizations/<lproj>/InfoPlist.strings`, restating `NSHumanReadableCopyright` as `Aqua Special Build. …` for the About pane); those overrides sit outside `Sources/Installer_macOS/` because that directory is an Xcode synchronized root group and a new `.lproj`-bearing sibling would be swept into the modern installer's resources.
- **Legacy Swift 5.10 path**: an additional, local-only path — the Swift 5.10 toolchain with the `MacOSX13.3.sdk` that **Command Line Tools** carries (`/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX13.3.sdk` — `LEGACY_SDK` names it; Xcode 15's copy is only a symlink, and current CLTs ship a *remover* for that legacy SDK instead, so a fresh machine must supply it), targeting `x86_64-apple-macosx10.9` (the deployment floor is **macOS 10.9** and is not negotiable: supporting it is the only reason this path exists — `legacyDeploymentTarget` in `Plugins/BundleAppsLegacy/plugin.swift`, `LEGACY_X86_TRIPLE` in the root `Makefile` and `LEGACY_TRIPLE` in all 20 per-package makefiles all say 10.9, and every legacy artifact must report 10.9 for `LSMinimumSystemVersion`/`minos`/`sdk`; holding it costs three `#available(macOS 10.10, *)` guards, all in `vChewing_SettingsUI`; the arm64 slice stays at 11.0, arm64's floor), with an old-enough **Xcode** as the active developer directory (the pin is Xcode 15.4; any Xcode whose *default* SDK is ≤ 14.x — i.e. ≤ 15.4 — is equivalent, and neither CLT nor a hand-made developer directory can stand in for it, both measured on 2026-09-16: `--sdk` never reaches build-plugin compilation). When an AppKit API sits above the floor, copy `vChewing-OSX-Legacy`'s shape — that repo is the 10.9-compliant reference — and never raise the floor instead. It does **not** replace the authoritative Swift 6.4+ / macOS 12+ setup (Swift 6.2 and 6.3 are deliberately blocked by per-package blocker manifests). Subpackages stop at static `.a` archives; the **repo root** is the one 5.10 manifest that produces executables — `vChewing` and `vChewingInstallerLegacy`, both force-loading `LegacyZone/ARCLite/libarclite_macosx.a` (the Swift driver never injects libArcLite, and `-L` + `-larclite_macosx` alone is inert). Under this rollout each subpackage carries `Package@swift-5.10.swift` plus `Package@swift-6.0` / `6.1` / `6.2` / `6.3` blocker manifests and its own lowercase `makefile` (`make build510`, `make clean510`); the LibVanguard aggregate's set — six manifests — is the reference implementation of that layout. Swift 5.10 builds stay out of CI: each runner would have to install the extra toolchain and the Xcode 15 SDK at no small cost, and the 5.10 side only serves local compilability and legacy-runtime-assembly verification. Three traps live only on this path: pass `{}` — never `nil` — to `setEventHandler`, because the embedded Swift 5.0 Dispatch shim forwards `nil` straight to `dispatch_source_set_event_handler(source, NULL)` and 10.9's libdispatch BUGs on a NULL block (SIGILL; this made `vChewingInstallerLegacy` crash seconds after pressing Install until 2026-09-16, while the modern runtime tolerates NULL and showed nothing); `LEGACY_SDK`'s `MacOSX13.3.sdk` is a **symlink** to the Command Line Tools copy, since Xcode 15 bundles macOS 14 — recreate it the same way on a fresh machine; and lexicon assets now build themselves, because `bundleLegacy` depends on the `lexiconLegacy` target, which runs `LegacyZone/LexiconBuildTrigger` with `LEXICON_CONFIG=release` (deliberately not `LEGACY_CONFIG`, which names the *app* configuration and leaks into sub-makes as a target-specific variable). Rollout details: `vChewing-DevLogs/Research/Phase217_SOP.md` (where that SOP is silent, `AGENTS.md` governs; conflicts escalate rather than being resolved silently).
- **Xcode cannot resolve Swift packages with an externally installed (OpenSource) toolchain**: resolution always runs on the toolchain Xcode itself ships, with no setting to delegate it. Since the manifest declares `swift-tools-version: 6.4` and Intel Macs top out at Xcode 26.x (< 6.4), **Xcode is no longer a usable build entry point on Intel Macs** — build through the SwiftPM CLI (`make spmDebug` / `make release`) against a 6.4+ toolchain instead (the legacy path was already CLI-driven, so it is unaffected). Apple silicon is unaffected: Xcode 27 ships Swift 6.4.
- **Resource lookup**: `MainAssembly4Darwin` uses custom `Bundle.currentSPM` accessor (`BundleAccessor.swift`) to locate factory lexicons from `.app/Contents/Resources/` (not `.app/` root) to avoid codesign sandbox violations.

## Things to Beware / Avoid
- When implementing new APIs for InputSession and InputHandler, please put them onto the protocols if possible. For shared session-management logic (state transitions, handler reset), prefer `SessionCoreProtocol` (defined in LibVanguard, `Session/SessionCoreProtocol.swift`) which provides default implementations of `switchState()` and `resetInputHandler()` shared between mock tests and production code. The session system is OS-independent: `InputSession`/`SessionProtocol` and the IMEState factories live in `vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard`'s `Session/` subdirectory; all OS-dependent actions (LXMgr, IMEApp, Notifier, AppDelegate, NS*, IMKHelper, etc.) are injected via `SessionHost` closures (see `SessionHost.swift` + `MainAssembly4Darwin/SessionHostWiring.swift`), with a Darwin surface (`InputSession_DarwinSurface.swift`) holding the IMK-facing entry points.
- Gate new APIs with availability checks (e.g. conditional compilation via `canImport(Darwin)` and Swift `@available` annotations) so shared packages keep compiling on Linux. The shipping Xcode target requires macOS 12+, but legacy macOS releases are maintained in a separate repository.
- This repo has no dependency of InterfaceBuilder assets. AppKit is used by default with self-crafted result builder DSLs to make the coding experience similar to SwiftUI. SwiftUI is used for the installer app (`./Packages/vChewing_InstallerAssembly4Darwin/`) and the macOS 14+ settings surface `SettingsUI` in `./Packages/vChewing_SettingsUI/` (which also hosts the phrase editor and the About pane); everything else stays AppKit. On macOS 12 Monterey and macOS 13 Ventura (i.e. below macOS 14), this repo uses SettingsCocoa (AppKit Result Builder DSL); on macOS 14 Sonoma and later it defaults to the SwiftUI SettingsUI (the Swift Observation macro it relies on requires macOS 14+), with SettingsCocoa kept as an AppKit alternate.
- User data is not expected to be referred from hard-coded path, unless it is necessary in Test targets of a Swift package.
- This repository uses Swift Testing / XCTest for unit tests among Swift packages situated in `./Packages` folder. Unit tests are **not** open to the Swift 5.10 legacy path: its manifests declare no test targets and the per-package `makefile`s expose no test goals. Tests run on the 6.4+ side only.
- Do not manually edit or commit generated lexicon assets; they are transient build artifacts produced by the `VanguardTextMapPlugin` build tool plugin at compile-time.
- The platforms in Swift package manifest file is ignored on non-Darwin platforms. Swift FOSS Foundation APIs on Darwin can be unavailable on earlier macOS releases due to Apple's deliberate intention of never backporting new Foundation APIs. Your removal of platforms can make some of those components not able to be compiled against macOS releases earlier than macOS 11. Exception for the Swift 5.10 legacy path: those version-selection manifests deliberately declare `platforms: nil` — the lowest macOS value PackageDescription accepts is 10.10, and declaring one would write that value into the artifact, which is wrong for both halves of that path: the subpackages ship static `.a` archives that carry no load command at all, and the repo-root executables must take their deployment target from the SDK plus the makefile's `-Xswiftc -target x86_64-apple-macosx10.9` override rather than from a platform declaration. The caution above applies to the 6.4+ shipping manifest (`.macOS(.v12)`) only.
- Most vChewing-specific packages prefer to use a dedicated file to handle `@_exported import XXX` dependency definitions to avoid insertion of `import XXX` to all files having codes dependent to `XXX`. This makes code-mirroring tasks (to the legacy repository of vChewing) much easier. Try not to break this convention if possible.
- Always confirm the current type of shell you are using (e.g., `powershell` or `zsh` or `bash`) before executing shell commands / writing shell scripts.
- If your current environment is macOS, please hesitate your use of python3 scripts unless being specifically told. Instead, prioritize powershell scripts or csharp scripts while running on macOS. If both powershell and csharp scripts are not available, you can use Swift scripts as the last resort. If Swift can't do it, use `python3` in lieu of `python`.

## Reference Files and Folders
- `./Packages/vChewing_MainAssembly4Darwin/Sources/MainAssembly4Darwin/SessionController/`: `InputSession_DarwinSurface.swift` hosts the IMK-facing surface (controller binding, NSEvent→KBEvent conversion, `recognizedEvents`/`showPreferences`/IMKInputController surface, `toggleInputMode` TIS logic); `SessionControllerSputnik.swift` binds it to IMK's `IMKInputSessionController` (from `vChewing_IMKUtils`), working with candidate window, IME settings, etc.; `SessionHostWiring.swift` injects `SessionHost` closures.
- `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/`: The typing module `InputHandler` protocol working with the IMEStateProtocol-based finite state machine. Also hosts the OS-independent session system in the `Session/` subdirectory: `SessionCoreProtocol` (shared session state-transition logic `switchState()`/`resetInputHandler()` with default implementations), `SessionProtocol` + `InputSession` (the session class), `IMEState` factories / `IMEStateParsed`, `SessionClientProxy` (cross-platform client-proxy abstraction), and `SessionHost` (host-injection point for all OS-dependent actions).
- `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/Sources/LexiconAssembly/`: Language model assembly (factory lexicon, user phrases, perceptor (LX_Perceptor), associated phrases).
- `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/Sources/Homa/`: The current sentence assembler used by LibVanguard and MainAssembly.
- `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/Sources/Tekkon/`: The phonabet composer designed for Chinese Phonabet (Zhuyin, Bopomofo) pronunciation data.
- `./Packages/vChewing_OSNeutral_LibVanguard/Deps/VanguardSwiftExtension/`: the general-purpose `SwiftExtension` utilities, kept as a **nested subpackage** inside the aggregate's directory (SwiftPM accepts nested packages) so that `.package(path:)` resolves identically here and in the `vChewing-LibVanguard` repository and the two manifests stay byte-identical. Package and product name `VanguardSwiftExtension`; module/target name `SwiftExtension`.
- `./Packages/vChewing_MainAssembly4Darwin/`: The sole module imported to the Xcode project. It integrates everything together. Real-simulation of typing experiences are handled in the unit tests of this package.
- `./Packages/vChewing_SettingsUI/`: Standalone preferences package — SwiftUI `SettingsUI` (macOS 14+) and AppKit `SettingsCocoa`, incl. the phrase editor UI; host actions are injected via `SettingsUIHost` closures (see `MainAssembly4Darwin/SettingsUIHostWiring.swift`).
